title: Assign each component's layer from its artifact type and responsibility

facts.note: Fires while the planner authors or revises component entries; the planning phase must be exposed by the harness.

Illustrative examples only, not an exhaustive gate: any planner artifact that declares a component with an artifact type, responsibility or layer qualifies. The source does not define a file-kind classifier.
Diff-level fact: a component entry is added, its layer/artifact type/responsibility is edited, or an existing placement is being reviewed.
Task text mentions components, their responsibility or layer placement.
Validator test_component_layer_assignment reports a component whose layer is outside its artifact type's typical layers.

fires: Planner adds an event-publisher component and must choose its layer
Planner declares a state-tracker component and sets its layer
Planner changes a config component's layer or artifact type
Planner changes a component's responsibility (e.g. a data component goes from coordinating a workflow to persisting to a store), so its existing placement must be reassessed
Planner reviews existing component placements in a plan
Validator flags an external event publisher assigned to the domain layer
doesNotFire: Coder edits implementation code without touching planned component layer assignments
Planner edits acceptance wording that changes neither the component's responsibility nor its artifact type or layer
Checking that a component has exactly one layer (covered by planner.component.layer-consistency)

given: A planned component has an artifact type (events, states, data or configs) and a responsibility.
when: The planner assigns, changes or reassesses its layer, or its responsibility changes.
then: Assign a layer from the artifact type's typical layers, chosen by responsibility: events → integration|application; states → domain|application; data → domain|application|integration; configs → application|integration.
prefer: Events (publishers sit at boundaries): publishing to external systems → integration; emitting internal events → application.
States: tracking core business state → domain; coordinating state/lifecycle → application.
Data (spans layers by responsibility): business logic → domain; coordinating the workflow → application; persisting to a store → integration.
Configs: coordinating setup → application; loading settings (e.g. from an external config store) → integration.
Treat the mapping as the default, defensible placement, not an absolute prohibition: the rule is advisory (severity 2) — findings are reported but do not block.
avoid: Placing an external event publisher in the domain layer.
Deciding the layer case by case or from the component name alone, ignoring its responsibility.
why: A typical-layer mapping per artifact type gives a default, defensible placement for each component, so layer assignment is consistent rather than guessed case by case.
evidence: Validator test_component_layer_assignment::test_component_layer_assignment passes for the plan's components (advisory: failures are reported, not blocking).

Each component's layer is in its artifact type's typical_layers set and the stated responsibility matches the chosen layer (boundary/external or settings loading/persistence → integration, coordination → application, core business state/logic → domain).
Compliant example: a state tracker placed at backend.domain. Non-compliant: an external event publisher placed at backend.domain.
verifier_detail: Typical-layer mapping by term_id: events_layers=[integration, application]; states_layers=[domain, application]; data_layers=[domain, application, integration]; configs_layers=[application, integration].
Layers are written qualified by side, e.g. backend.domain, backend.application, backend.integration; compare the layer suffix against typical_layers.
Term labels: events_layers 'Layers for event components'; states_layers 'Layers for state components'; data_layers 'Layers for data components'; configs_layers 'Layers for config components'.

Term rationales: events 'Event publishers at boundaries (external integration or internal application)'; states 'State trackers manage business state (domain) or coordinate (application)'; data 'Data handlers span layers based on responsibility'; configs 'Configuration components coordinate setup or load settings'.
Source illustrative examples (events): MatchStartedPublisher → backend.integration (publishes to external systems); StateCommittedEmitter → backend.application (emits internal events).
Source illustrative examples (states): TimebankTracker → backend.domain (tracks core business state); SessionManager → backend.application (coordinates session lifecycle).

Source illustrative examples (data): ChoiceMaker → backend.domain (business logic for making choice); ChoiceHandler → backend.application (coordinates choice workflow); ChoicePersister → backend.integration (persists to database).

Source illustrative examples (configs): MatchConfigurator → backend.application (coordinates match setup); ConfigLoader → backend.integration (loads from external config store). The external store is an example; loading settings in general maps to integration.
Disposition advisory, severity 2: findings are reported but do not block.
